- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to smoothly decay toward historical averages after spikes.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) show underestimation, possibly due to lagging data or model not capturing tail risks.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the 30-day forecast, especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, then fails to adjust downward.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high, especially when recent history shows strong upward trend.
- Model underestimates true outcomes in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting it doesn’t account for late-stage momentum or policy-driven price corrections.
